name: sisc-scheme
why: A full Scheme implementation in Java with continuations and serialization, an old-school oddity worth an afternoon of poking.

brief.what_it_is: SISC (Second Interpreter of Scheme Code) is a Scheme interpreter written in Java. Per its homepage, it takes Scheme source and runs it on the JVM, and it claims to be a complete implementation of R5RS with a full numeric tower (complex, arbitrary-precision integers, floating point), hygienic macros, proper tail recursion, and first-class continuations. It also ships extras: networking, exception handling, a module system, SLIB support, several SRFIs, and a Java foreign-function interface. The homepage does not mention serialization, which the scout notes attribute to it.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage frames SISC as a fast, standards-faithful Scheme for the JVM: it says SISC "uses modern interpretation techniques, and handily outperforms all existing JVM interpreters (often by more than an order of magnitude)" while still implementing the standard "as correctly as possible."
brief.how_it_works: The homepage gives no implementation detail beyond calling it an interpreter that uses "modern interpretation techniques." Native functionality is added through Modules, which can add types, values, and functions and can be packaged into scopable modules at the Scheme level.
brief.install_notes: The homepage lists downloads: a Full distribution (.zip, .tar.gz, .deb, and source) and a Lite distribution (.zip, .tar.gz), plus CVS access. The newest listed release is 1.16.6 dated 2007-02-27. The homepage does not describe JVM version requirements, classpath setup, or a first-run step. The brew formula's executable is named sisc. Documentation, the wiki, and an online trial are linked from the page, but I did not follow them and their URLs are not visible in the fetched text.
brief.standout: A pre-2010 Scheme that claims full R5RS compliance with first-class continuations on the JVM, dual-licensed under MPL 1.1 and GPL v2, and packaged with a Java foreign-function interface and a module system. Its own comparison page and benchmark claims make it an interesting time capsule of early JVM Scheme implementations.
brief.status: Quiet. The newest release on the homepage is 1.16.6 from 2007-02-27, the copyright line reads 2001-2007, and the support section points to a SourceForge project and an IRC channel on freenode. I found no sign of later releases or recent activity. I did not check the SourceForge page or repository history.
brief.caveats: Release dates and the copyright line both date the project to about 2007, so expect old JVM and Java compatibility questions and no modern packaging. The homepage has no installation instructions. The scout note's mention of serialization is not confirmed by the homepage. The homepage's performance and R5RS claims are the authors' own and I did not verify them.
quotes: SISC is an extensible Java based interpreter of the algorithmic language Scheme.
SISC is a complete implementation of the language. The entire R5RS Scheme standard is supported, no exceptions.
SISC is released simultaneously under the terms of the Mozilla Public License (MPL) v1.1 and the GNU General Public License (GPL) v2.
